What's the minimum committed capacity for Dedicated reseller margins?

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-04
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (CTO, Hawthorn), Nina Gomez (Head of Cloud), Elias Park (Infra)
---
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick round robin?
[00:18] Samir Patel: yeah, thanks. samir here, CTO at Hawthorn. we run hybrid workloads across aws and a modest on-prem cluster, looking at reselling GPU capacity to some of our customers.
[00:35] Nina Gomez: nina - head of cloud. major ask is we need a resale model that fits our billing and also integrates with our tenant isolation.
[00:50] Maya Chen: great. Diego (SE) is going to go through architecture options, i'll cover partner commercial stuff. this is meant to be exploratory, figure out a pilot scope.
[01:12] Diego Alvarez: hi all, uh quick note - sometimes i call the Redwood Dedicated product "Redwood Dedi" in notes, so don't be surprised. high level: three models - hosted (redwood cloud endpoint), dedicated pool (reserved gpus in our infra), private (V P C / on-prem).
[01:40] Elias Park: for the pilot we were thinking dedicated reseller pools so we can keep customer data isolated, but open to hosted if network and S L A work.
[02:05] Diego Alvarez: sounds reasonable. dedicated gives you predictable throughput and easier margining for resale, hosted is faster to launch but harder to isolate at the tenant level.
[02:32] Samir Patel: margin math is key. we need to know minimal commit and typical utilization to see if resale holds up. also procurement wants SOC2, S S O and audit logs.
[02:50] Maya Chen: we have enterprise add-ons - SOC 2 docs, SAML SSO, and extended audit retention. i'll send the pack after the call.
[03:06] Nina Gomez: quick question on keys - can you support customer-managed KMS? some of our finance customers force keys.
[03:19] Diego Alvarez: yes, we support customer K M S via our Private deployment model and there are options for H S M in dedicated as well but that requires extra config. note that sometimes the transcript has "K M S" split out in our docs, sorry if weird.
[03:45] Samir Patel: network - we need V P C peering to our account and cross-account role. any gotchas there?
[03:55] Diego Alvarez: V P C peering is supported for Private and for Dedicated we can do V P C peering + NAT routing. the only thing to watch for is egress paths for monitoring and if you want to host the control plane on your side there's a different runbook.
[04:25] Nina Gomez: what's the kernel selection / model support? we run Lama 2 and some finetuned open models.
[04:35] Diego Alvarez: we support Llama-2 family (sometimes spelled Lama 2 in notes), Bloom, and MPT builds. our runtime picks kernels per arch and we have quantized paths. for finetuned models we'd recommend binding a model version for the pilot.
[05:02] Samir Patel: benchmark — we want to see latency at 8k context for convo gen and throughput for 100 rps of short prompts, roughly.
[05:20] Diego Alvarez: good. propose a 2-hour benchark: run hosted and dedicated configs, measure p95 latency and GPU utilization. i'll put together a config sheet.
[05:40] Samir Patel: when can that happen?
[05:44] Diego Alvarez: next week or the week after — depends on data prep from you for realistic traffic.
[06:01] Nina Gomez: also need to see monitoring hooks - prometheus metrics, token-level cost, and tracing.
[06:12] Diego Alvarez: Redwood Console exposes token-level cost and lat breakdown by model and route; for dedicated we can stream traces to your prometheus/tempo stack.
[06:33] Samir Patel: procurement will ask about reseller contract language, indemnity, and SLAs.
[06:43] Maya Chen: we'll share standard reseller T&Cs and highlight where we can flex. initial pilots usually run 3 months with an option to convert to a committed monthly capacity.
[07:00] Elias Park: curious about KV cache behavior — if we do multi-tenant, can we ensure no KV leakage?
[07:12] Diego Alvarez: good callout. runtime isolates KV caches per model instance and we have prefix caching options; we'll document the isolation guarantees. sometimes my notes say "KV chache" — sorry.
[07:34] Samir Patel: security review — do you provide penetration test reports and SOC 2 Type 2?
[07:42] Maya Chen: yes, SOC2 Type 2 available and we can provide pen test summary; full reports under NDA.
[07:55] Nina Gomez: timeline — we're planning a Q1 pilot for a couple of key customers. procurement not great on short turnarounds, so 6 weeks to get contracts in order would be ideal.
[08:12] Maya Chen: noted. usual flow: share pricing -> legal review -> pilot SOW -> benchark -> exec signoff.
[08:25] Diego Alvarez: architecture options quick dive: option A: Redwood Hosted reseller model - fastest but limits tenant isolation; option B: Dedicated reseller pool - best for margins and isolation; option C: Private (V P C) - tightest control and K M S support but longest lead time.
[09:00] Elias Park: lead time numbers?
[09:05] Diego Alvarez: hosted: days; dedicated: 2-4 weeks for pool provisioning and config; private: 6-8 weeks with network and key provisioning.
[09:22] Samir Patel: cost signaling? rough numbers ok.
[09:26] Maya Chen: i'll share a partner pricing spreadsheet with tiered margins. rough gist: hosted per-token cost is higher but no infra commit; dedicated has lower unit cost with commit.
[09:41] Nina Gomez: any competitor differentiation? we've looked at NebulaCloud and ApexFusion, both had different billing models.
[09:50] Maya Chen: compared to NebulaCloud we push on observability and predictable latency; vs ApexFusion we differ in unified tooling across hosted/dedicated/private.
[10:10] Diego Alvarez: technical note: caching and batching decisions will affect latency and cost. we can show a sample config that balances p95 vs unit cost.
[10:30] Samir Patel: ok for benchark inputs we'll give you the token distribution and sample prompts.
[10:38] Diego Alvarez: perfect. benchark plan items: model versions to test, sequence lengths, concurrency, warmup, and trace capture points. i'll email the template.
[11:00] Nina Gomez: curious about SSO - SAML or OIDC?
[11:06] Maya Chen: both supported, SAML is common for enterprise. we support identity federation and RBAC.
[11:20] Elias Park: monitoring retention - can we keep logs longer for compliance?
[11:26] Diego Alvarez: yes, extended retention is an add-on. we also can stream logs to your SIEM.
[11:45] Samir Patel: any gotchas with on-prem GPUs? we have some older A100s and some new H100s.
[11:55] Diego Alvarez: heterogenous fleets are ok but performance profiles will vary; for pilot we should pin model to a specific hardware class to avoid noisy neighbor effects.
[12:12] Maya Chen: business question — reselling or white-labeling? what are you aiming for?
[12:19] Samir Patel: primary resell under our brand but note Redwood as technology partner in docs.
[12:26] Maya Chen: understood. there are MSA and reseller addenda we can adapt.
[12:40] Nina Gomez: let's talk about PKI - we need cert rotation automation for peering endpoints.
[12:49] Diego Alvarez: that's supported via our automation runner; will include in runbook.
[13:05] Samir Patel: can we do a short pilot SOW example on the call?
[13:12] Maya Chen: yep - typical pilot SOW: 3 months, defined test customers, success metrics (p95 < X ms, cost per 1k tokens < $Y), deliverables include benchark report and runbook.
[13:30] Elias Park: success metrics: p95 < 200ms for short prompts, p95 < 800ms for 8k context, and throughput target 100 rps for bursty traffic.
[13:45] Diego Alvarez: we'll try to align to that in benchark.
[14:00] Maya Chen: procurement will also want termination and data handling clauses; we have standard language.
[14:10] Samir Patel: any pre-reqs for benchark? we can provide OAuth tokens and sample data.
[14:18] Diego Alvarez: need traffic shape, sample prompts, model versions, expected concurrency, and a contact for infra.
[14:30] Nina Gomez: ok we'll assemble that.
[14:38] Maya Chen: next steps recap later in the call - but immediate: maya sends pricing, diego sends benchark template, elias sends utilization csv.
[14:52] Samir Patel: sounds good.
[15:02] Diego Alvarez: quick technical deep-dive note — if you want to run quantized models on older A100s that's fine but you'll see different perf; we'll flag model-specific recommendations.
[15:20] Elias Park: fair.
[15:30] Nina Gomez: one more security question - do you support customer managed audit logs separated by tenant?
[15:40] Diego Alvarez: yes, per-tenant audit exports and we can push to your S3 or SIEM.
[15:52] Samir Patel: ok, timeline again - benchark next week is preferred; procurement wants 6 weeks to sign pilot.
[16:05] Maya Chen: we'll aim to turn around pricing and docs in 3 business days. benchark scheduling for week-of 2026-12-14 pending your data.
[16:20] Samir Patel: ok.
[16:25] Nina Gomez: any trial credits for partners?
[16:29] Maya Chen: we have partner credits for initial bencharks; i'll include numbers in the spreadsheet.
[16:40] Diego Alvarez: i'll also include recommended quant profiles and batch settings to help you hit latency targets.
[16:55] Samir Patel: good.
[17:05] Maya Chen: on legal - we can provide reseller addendum and sample SOW for review.
[17:15] Samir Patel: who's the right contact at Redwood for legal?
[17:18] Maya Chen: i'll cc our partnerships legal contact in the email.
[17:30] Diego Alvarez: tech note - if you want to do an on-prem private deployment later, expect more wiring: peering, certs, K M S, and an ops runbook.
[17:45] Elias Park: yeah that's fine.
[18:00] Maya Chen: we should also flag competitors - they asked about NebulaCloud and ApexFusion - i'll include a short comparison doc.
[18:10] Samir Patel: any red flags from Redwood side?
[18:14] Maya Chen: nothing big; must align on pilot scope and success metrics to ensure it's feasible.
[18:25] Nina Gomez: ok, let's lock on dates.
[18:30] Maya Chen: action items and due dates on the summary. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the deck and benchark template.
